findings.english_quote: Hermas advocates self-limitation for others’ good; the rendering preserves the literal semantics of ἐνδεής (lacking) while signaling voluntary posture.
findings.issue: The theological metadata asserts a beneficiary and motive—“for others’ good”—that this clause does not state. The surrounding service list supplies context, but does not establish that specific purpose for this instruction. The lexical rationale similarly asserts “self‑limitation for others’ sake.” This is an added explanatory claim, not a defect requiring replacement of the disclosed working reading or the main-text rendering.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove the asserted other-directed motive from both rationales. A proposed rationale is: “The rendering takes ἐνδεέστερον as having less or being more in need and retains the comparison with all other people. The instruction does not explicitly state its purpose or beneficiaries.” Submit any revised rationale for fresh review.

findings.english_quote: Hermas advocates self-limitation for others’ good; the rendering preserves the literal semantics of ἐνδεής (lacking) while signaling voluntary posture.
findings.issue: Independently of the standard edition, the simplified edition’s theological metadata adds the unstated purpose “for others’ good.” Its lexical rationale also supplies “for others’ sake.” Neither purpose is expressed in the selected clause. The simplified reader text retains the comparative instruction without that addition.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove the unsupported beneficiary and motive from the theological and lexical rationales. Describe the selected lacking/need interpretation and the comparison with everyone without asserting why the instruction is given. Any replacement metadata requires fresh review.

summary: Both reader texts cover the selected source’s clauses, retain its difficult good/evil contrast, necessity, negations, salvation language, and both concluding conditions. Both follow the working paragraph-6 speaker division, use reader-facing “servant,” and disclose editorial supplements and substantive alternatives rather than harmonizing them. Revision is needed for an unsupported motive asserted in both editions’ metadata. This is a model review of the supplied working source and English, not certification of the external editions, plate readings, handwriting, or exhaustive collation cited in the notes; those external claims remain unverified here. No repentance terminology occurs in this unit.
